summary: When Ask lays components out as a table, the header naming each state now reads in full on the canvas. A copy's violet name chip that would have printed over those words stays off until you point at or pick that copy.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walks: ask-builds-base-components-walk (the real Ask request) and component-sheet-chips-clear-walk (the same kind of sheet built in five seconds).

try.do: On a blank picture, press Ask and type: create a table of apple like quality base components that show different states and text.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click bare canvas so nothing is picked, and read the headers across the top of each row.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Rest the pointer on the Hover button.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click it, then move the pointer away.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Compare with the sheet from 2026-10-24, where Hover, Pressed and Disabled were half covered.

evaluate: Do the headers and the drawings read as a clean table at the zoom it opens at?
With no chips at rest, can you still tell which drawings are linked copies of a component?
When you point at a copy, is it fine that its chip sits over the header until you move away?
rough: At rest a copy under a header shows no mark at all, so nothing on the canvas says it is a linked copy until you point at it. The Layers list still marks each one with a violet diamond and its version.
The rule is general: any component chip that would print over any words in the picture is left off at rest, not only on Ask's sheets. A screen's own name chip is unchanged.
A picked copy's chip still sits close above its top resize handle, as it did before this change.
No mock covers the chips over a component sheet.
